chapters.title: Unit 1: Rational Numbers and Decimal Numbers

lessons.title: Getting Started — Integers in Daily Life
lessons.notes_html:
Question 1. Think! Give any five real life examples in which you use negative integers.

Answer: Negative integers are used wherever a value is counted below a zero reference point.
(i) Temperature below 0 <sup>o</sup>C in winter, for example -5 <sup>o</sup>C.
(ii) Floors below ground level in a building, for example basement -1 and -2.
(iii) Depth below sea level, for example a fish at -750 ft.
(iv) Money owed or borrowed, for example a debt of Rs. 500 written as -500.
(v) A drop in marks or points, for example losing 10 points written as -10.

Question 2. Skill Practice: Solve the following: |-10|, |-17|, |19| and |-6|. Also arrange them in ascending and descending order.

Step 1: The absolute value |x| is the distance of x from 0 on the number line, so it is never negative.
Step 2: |-10| = 10, because -10 is 10 units away from 0.
Step 3: |-17| = 17, because -17 is 17 units away from 0.
Step 4: |19| = 19, because 19 is 19 units away from 0.
Step 5: |-6| = 6, because -6 is 6 units away from 0.
Step 6: Ascending order (smallest to largest): 6, 10, 17, 19.
Step 7: Descending order (largest to smallest): 19, 17, 10, 6.
Final answer: |-10| = 10, |-17| = 17, |19| = 19, |-6| = 6; ascending 6, 10, 17, 19; descending 19, 17, 10, 6.

Question 3. Skill Practice: Represent the following whole numbers on the number line: (i) 880, 730, 540, 990, 670.

Step 1: All five numbers lie between 500 and 1000, so draw a number line from 500 to 1000 with equal gaps of 100.
Step 2: Mark 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 and 1000 at equal distances.
Step 3: 540 lies between 500 and 600, close to 500.
Step 4: 670 lies between 600 and 700, close to 700.
Step 5: 730 lies between 700 and 800, close to 700.
Step 6: 880 lies between 800 and 900, close to 900.
Step 7: 990 lies between 900 and 1000, very close to 1000.
Final answer in ascending order on the line: 540, 670, 730, 880, 990.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of a negative integer used in daily life?
options: A temperature of -5 degrees C in winter
A temperature of 25 degrees C in summer
mcqs.why: Negative integers count values below a zero reference point. A temperature of -5 degrees C is 5 degrees below zero, so it uses a negative integer.

mcqs.q: What is the value of |-10|?
mcqs.why: Absolute value is the distance from 0 on the number line. |-10| = 10 because -10 is 10 units away from 0, and distance is never negative.

mcqs.q: What is the value of |-17|?
mcqs.why: Absolute value is the distance from 0. |-17| = 17 because -17 is 17 units away from 0 on the number line.

mcqs.q: What is the value of |19|?
mcqs.why: Absolute value is the distance from 0. |19| = 19 because 19 is 19 units away from 0, and it is already positive.

mcqs.q: What is the value of |-6|?
mcqs.why: Absolute value is the distance from 0. |-6| = 6 because -6 is 6 units away from 0 on the number line.

mcqs.q: What is the ascending order of |-10|, |-17|, |19| and |-6|?
mcqs.why: First find the values: |-10| = 10, |-17| = 17, |19| = 19 and |-6| = 6. Arranging 6, 10, 17, 19 from smallest to largest gives 6, 10, 17, 19.

mcqs.q: What is the descending order of |-10|, |-17|, |19| and |-6|?
mcqs.why: The values are |-10| = 10, |-17| = 17, |19| = 19 and |-6| = 6. Arranging them from largest to smallest gives 19, 17, 10, 6.

mcqs.q: A debt of Rs. 500 is written as which integer?
mcqs.why: Money owed or borrowed is counted below zero, so it is written with a negative sign. A debt of Rs. 500 is written as -500.

mcqs.q: A fish at -750 ft is at which position?
mcqs.why: Depth below sea level is written as a negative integer. The value -750 ft means the fish is 750 ft below the zero reference of sea level.

mcqs.q: On a number line from 500 to 1000, 540 lies between which two marked hundreds?
mcqs.why: The number 540 is greater than 500 and less than 600, so on the line it lies between 500 and 600, close to 500.

lessons.title: Challenge — The 7-Digit Number Puzzle
lessons.notes_html:
Challenge — Find the 7-digit number with the help of the given clues: 2 is at ones place. The place value of 1 is 100. 7 is not at the tens place. 4 is at thousand place. The digit at the hundred thousands place is sum of digits at thousands and ones place. The digit at ten thousands is one more than the digit at thousand place. 7 digits are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 to make a 7-digit number.

Step 1: Write the seven places from the left: millions, hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones.
Step 2: Ones place = 2 (given).
Step 3: Place value of 1 is 100, so 1 is at the hundreds place.
Step 4: Thousands place = 4 (given).
Step 5: Hundred thousands place = thousands digit + ones digit = 4 + 2 = 6.
Step 6: Ten thousands place = thousands digit + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5.
Step 7: Digits used so far are 2, 1, 4, 6, 5. The digits left from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7} are 3 and 7, for the millions and tens places.
Step 8: 7 is NOT at the tens place, so tens place = 3 and millions place = 7.
Step 9: Fill the places in order: millions 7, hundred thousands 6, ten thousands 5, thousands 4, hundreds 1, tens 3, ones 2.
Final answer: 7,654,132.

mcqs.q: In the 7-digit number puzzle, which digit is at the ones place?
mcqs.why: The first clue states directly that 2 is at the ones place, so the ones digit of the 7-digit number is 2.

mcqs.q: In the puzzle, the place value of 1 is 100. At which place is the digit 1?
mcqs.why: A digit with place value 100 sits at the hundreds place. Since the place value of 1 is 100, the digit 1 is at the hundreds place.

mcqs.q: In the puzzle, which digit is at the thousands place?
mcqs.why: The clues state directly that 4 is at the thousand place, so the thousands digit of the number is 4.

mcqs.q: The digit at the hundred thousands place is the sum of the digits at the thousands and ones places. What is it?
mcqs.why: Working: thousands digit + ones digit = 4 + 2 = 6. So the hundred thousands digit is 6.

mcqs.q: The digit at the ten thousands place is one more than the digit at the thousand place. What is it?
mcqs.why: Working: thousands digit + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5. So the ten thousands digit is 5.

mcqs.q: In the puzzle, 7 is not at the tens place. Which digit is at the tens place?
mcqs.why: After placing 2, 1, 4, 6 and 5, the digits left are 3 and 7 for the millions and tens places. Since 7 is not at the tens place, the tens digit is 3.

mcqs.q: Which digit is at the millions place in the puzzle number?
mcqs.why: The digits left for millions and tens are 3 and 7. The tens place takes 3 because 7 is not at the tens place, so the millions place takes 7.

mcqs.q: What is the complete 7-digit number in the puzzle?
mcqs.why: Filling the places in order gives millions 7, hundred thousands 6, ten thousands 5, thousands 4, hundreds 1, tens 3, ones 2, which makes 7654132.

mcqs.q: After using the digits 2, 1, 4, 6 and 5, which two digits are left for the millions and tens places?
mcqs.why: The digits to use are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Removing the used digits 2, 1, 4, 6 and 5 leaves the digits 3 and 7.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 1 in the puzzle number?
mcqs.why: The clue gives the place value of 1 as 100, which also confirms that 1 sits at the hundreds place in the number 7654132.

lessons.title: Skill Practice — Integers on the Number Line
lessons.notes_html:
Skill Practice — Represent the following on the number line: (i) -700, 100, 900, -800, -500 (ii) 2200, -1800, -900, 1500, 2500.

Step 1: For part (i), draw a number line from -1000 to 1000 with equal gaps of 100.
Step 2: Mark -800 between -900 and -700, -700, -500, 100 and 900 in that left-to-right order.
Step 3: Ascending order (i): -800, -700, -500, 100, 900. Descending order (i): 900, 100, -500, -700, -800.
Step 4: For part (ii), draw a number line from -2000 to 3000 with equal gaps of 100.
Step 5: Mark -1800, -900, 1500, 2200 and 2500 in that left-to-right order.
Final answer (ii): ascending -1800, -900, 1500, 2200, 2500; descending 2500, 2200, 1500, -900, -1800.

Skill Practice — Represent the following integers on number line: -50, 60, -30, -20, 10, 40.

Step 1: Draw a number line from -60 to 70 with equal gaps of 10.
Step 2: Mark the numbers from left to right: -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60.
Final answer: ascending order -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60; descending order 60, 40, 10, -20, -30, -50.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest number in the set -700, 100, 900, -800, -500?
mcqs.why: On the number line the leftmost number is the smallest. In ascending order the set is -800, -700, -500, 100, 900, so the smallest is -800.

mcqs.q: What is the largest number in the set -700, 100, 900, -800, -500?
mcqs.why: On the number line the rightmost number is the largest. In ascending order the set is -800, -700, -500, 100, 900, so the largest is 900.

mcqs.q: What is the ascending order of -700, 100, 900, -800, -500?
mcqs.why: Numbers increase from left to right on the number line. Reading the marked points from left to right gives -800, -700, -500, 100, 900.

mcqs.q: For the set -700, 100, 900, -800, -500, a number line from -1000 to 1000 uses equal gaps of how much?
mcqs.why: The notes draw this line from -1000 to 1000 with equal gaps of 100, marking -800, -700, -500, 100 and 900 at those steps.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest number in the set 2200, -1800, -900, 1500, 2500?
mcqs.why: In ascending order the set is -1800, -900, 1500, 2200, 2500. The first, leftmost and smallest number is -1800.

mcqs.q: What is the descending order of 2200, -1800, -900, 1500, 2500?
mcqs.why: Descending order goes from largest to smallest. The largest is 2500, then 2200, 1500, -900, and the smallest is -1800.

mcqs.q: In the set -50, 60, -30, -20, 10, 40, which number is at the far left of the number line?
mcqs.why: In ascending order the set is -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60. The far left point is the smallest number, which is -50.

mcqs.q: What is the ascending order of -50, 60, -30, -20, 10, 40?
mcqs.why: Reading the points from left to right on a line from -60 to 70 gives -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60 in ascending order.

mcqs.q: What is the descending order of -50, 60, -30, -20, 10, 40?
mcqs.why: Descending order is the reverse of ascending order -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60, so it is 60, 40, 10, -20, -30, -50.

mcqs.q: On the number line for -50, 60, -30, -20, 10, 40, which number comes immediately after -20 when moving to the right?
mcqs.why: In left-to-right order the numbers are -50, -30, -20, 10, 40, 60. The number immediately to the right of -20 is 10.

lessons.title: Skill Practice — Ordering Decimal Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Skill Practice — Write the following integers on your notebook and arrange them in ascending and descending order: -890.550, -230.430, -410.890.

Step 1: All three numbers are negative, so the one farthest from zero is the smallest.
Step 2: Compare: -890.550 is farthest from zero, then -410.890, then -230.430 is closest to zero.
Final answer: ascending order -890.550, -410.890, -230.430; descending order -230.430, -410.890, -890.550.

mcqs.q: What is the ascending order of -890.550, -230.430, -410.890?
mcqs.why: All three numbers are negative, so the one farthest from zero is smallest. -890.550 is farthest, then -410.890, then -230.430, giving ascending order -890.550, -410.890, -230.430.

mcqs.q: What is the descending order of -890.550, -230.430, -410.890?
mcqs.why: Descending order is the reverse of ascending order. Since ascending is -890.550, -410.890, -230.430, descending is -230.430, -410.890, -890.550.

mcqs.q: Which of -890.550, -230.430, -410.890 is the smallest?
mcqs.why: For negative numbers, the one farthest from zero is the smallest. -890.550 is farthest from zero, so it is the smallest of the three.

mcqs.q: Which of -890.550, -230.430, -410.890 is the largest?
mcqs.why: For negative numbers, the one closest to zero is the largest. -230.430 is closest to zero, so it is the largest of the three numbers.

mcqs.q: Which sign correctly compares -890.550 and -410.890?
mcqs.why: Both are negative and -890.550 is farther from zero than -410.890, so -890.550 is smaller. Therefore -890.550 < -410.890.

mcqs.q: Which sign correctly compares -230.430 and -410.890?
mcqs.why: Both are negative and -230.430 is closer to zero than -410.890, so -230.430 is larger. Therefore -230.430 > -410.890.

mcqs.q: Which of -890.550, -230.430, -410.890 lies in the middle in ascending order?
mcqs.why: Ascending order is -890.550, -410.890, -230.430. The middle position is occupied by -410.890.

mcqs.q: For negative numbers, which statement is correct?
options: The number farthest from zero is the largest
The number farthest from zero is the smallest
The number closest to zero is the smallest
mcqs.why: The notes state that when all numbers are negative, the one farthest from zero is the smallest, and the one closest to zero is the largest.

mcqs.q: Using the same rule, what is the ascending order of -120.5, -45.5, -300.5?
mcqs.why: All are negative, so order by distance from zero: -300.5 is farthest and smallest, then -120.5, then -45.5 closest to zero. Ascending order is -300.5, -120.5, -45.5.

mcqs.q: Using the same rule, which is larger: -15.25 or -150.25?
mcqs.why: Both are negative. -15.25 is closer to zero than -150.25, and for negative numbers the one closer to zero is larger, so -15.25 is larger.

Question 2. Convert: (i) 1 2/3, 3 4/5, 2 5/10, 8 3/7 into improper fractions (ii) 18/7, 63/14, 43/13, 115/9 into mixed fractions.

Step 1: Mixed to improper: multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator.
Step 2: (i) 1 2/3 = (1 x 3 + 2)/3 = 5/3; 3 4/5 = (3 x 5 + 4)/5 = 19/5; 2 5/10 = (2 x 10 + 5)/10 = 25/10 = 5/2; 8 3/7 = (8 x 7 + 3)/7 = 59/7.
Step 3: Improper to mixed: divide the numerator by the denominator; the quotient is the whole part and the remainder over the denominator is the fraction.
Step 4: (ii) 18/7 = 2 4/7 (18 = 2 x 7 + 4); 63/14 = 4 7/14 = 4 1/2; 43/13 = 3 4/13 (43 = 3 x 13 + 4); 115/9 = 12 7/9 (115 = 12 x 9 + 7).
Final answer: (i) 5/3, 19/5, 25/10, 59/7 (ii) 2 4/7, 4 1/2, 3 4/13, 12 7/9.

mcqs.q: On the number line, 5/3 lies between which two integers?
mcqs.why: Working: 5/3 = 1 2/3, which is greater than 1 and less than 2, so 5/3 lies between 1 and 2 on the number line.

mcqs.q: On the number line, -3/5 lies between which two integers?
mcqs.why: The value -3/5 is negative but greater than -1, since -3/5 = -0.6. So it lies between -1 and 0 on the number line.

mcqs.q: Convert 1 2/3 into an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: (1 x 3 + 2)/3 = 5/3. So 1 2/3 = 5/3.

mcqs.q: Convert 3 4/5 into an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Working: (3 x 5 + 4)/5 = (15 + 4)/5 = 19/5. So 3 4/5 = 19/5 as an improper fraction.

mcqs.q: Convert 8 3/7 into an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Working: (8 x 7 + 3)/7 = (56 + 3)/7 = 59/7. So 8 3/7 = 59/7 as an improper fraction.

mcqs.q: Convert 18/7 into a mixed fraction.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 18 by 7: 18 = 2 x 7 + 4, so the quotient is 2 and the remainder is 4. Therefore 18/7 = 2 4/7.

mcqs.q: Convert 115/9 into a mixed fraction.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 115 by 9: 115 = 12 x 9 + 7, so the quotient is 12 and the remainder is 7. Therefore 115/9 = 12 7/9.

mcqs.q: Which sign correctly compares 3/5 and 6/25?
mcqs.why: Working: write 3/5 with denominator 25: 3/5 = 15/25. Since 15/25 > 6/25, we have 3/5 > 6/25.

mcqs.q: Which sign correctly compares -3/8 and -5/8?
mcqs.why: Both have denominator 8 and both are negative. -3/8 is closer to zero than -5/8, so -3/8 is larger: -3/8 > -5/8.

mcqs.q: What is the ascending order of 1/4, 3/5, 7/8, 1 1/4?
mcqs.why: Working with denominator 40: 1/4 = 10/40, 3/5 = 24/40, 7/8 = 35/40, 1 1/4 = 50/40. In size order this gives 1/4, 3/5, 7/8, 1 1/4.

lessons.title: Skill Practice — Operations on Rational Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Skill Practice — Solve the following: 1/2 + 7/9 + 1/9 = ?

Step 1: Add the fractions with the same denominator first: 7/9 + 1/9 = 8/9.
Step 2: Now add 1/2 + 8/9. The LCM of 2 and 9 is 18.
Step 3: 1/2 = 9/18 and 8/9 = 16/18.
Step 4: 9/18 + 16/18 = 25/18.
Final answer: 25/18 = 1 7/18.

Skill Practice — Danish purchased a cake. He eats 3/10 parts of the cake. Danish's friend eats 1/5 parts of the cake and his sister eats 4/15 parts of the cake. Can you find out how much cake is left with Danish?

Step 1: Total eaten = 3/10 + 1/5 + 4/15. The LCM of 10, 5 and 15 is 30.
Step 2: 3/10 = 9/30, 1/5 = 6/30, 4/15 = 8/30.
Step 3: 9/30 + 6/30 + 8/30 = 23/30.
Step 4: Cake left = 1 - 23/30 = 7/30.
Final answer: 7/30 of the cake is left.

Skill Practice — Solve the following: 11/15 - 9/15 - 2/15 = ?

Step 1: All three fractions have the same denominator 15, so subtract the numerators.
Step 2: 11 - 9 - 2 = 0.
Step 3: 0/15 = 0.
Final answer: 0.

Skill Practice — Find the additive inverse: (i) 2/3 (ii) -4/7.

Step 1: The additive inverse of a number is the same number with the opposite sign.
Step 2: (i) The additive inverse of 2/3 is -2/3, because 2/3 + (-2/3) = 0.
Step 3: (ii) The additive inverse of -4/7 is 4/7, because -4/7 + 4/7 = 0.
Final answer: (i) -2/3 (ii) 4/7.

Skill Practice — Ahmad's friend left 3/8 of a whole pizza for him, Ahmad ate 1/3 of what was left. How much of the whole pizza did Ahmad left?

Step 1: What was left for Ahmad = 3/8 of the pizza.
Step 2: Ahmad ate 1/3 of what was left: 1/3 x 3/8 = 3/24 = 1/8 of the whole pizza.
Step 3: What Ahmad left = 3/8 - 1/8 = 2/8.
Step 4: 2/8 = 1/4.
Final answer: 1/4 of the whole pizza was left.

Skill Practice — Solve the following: (2/3 x 9/10) / (3/10) = ?

Step 1: First multiply inside the brackets: 2/3 x 9/10 = 18/30 = 3/5.
Step 2: Now divide by 3/10: 3/5 / (3/10) = 3/5 x 10/3.
Step 3: 3/5 x 10/3 = 30/15 = 2.
Final answer: 2.

mcqs.q: Danish eats 3/10 of a cake, his friend eats 1/5 and his sister eats 4/15. How much cake is left?
mcqs.why: Working: total eaten with LCM 30 is 9/30 + 6/30 + 8/30 = 23/30. Cake left = 1 - 23/30 = 7/30.
Working: all fractions have denominator 15, so subtract the numerators: 11 - 9 - 2 = 0, giving 0/15 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the additive inverse of 2/3?
mcqs.why: The additive inverse has the opposite sign and sums to zero. The inverse of 2/3 is -2/3 because 2/3 + (-2/3) = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the additive inverse of -4/7?
mcqs.why: The additive inverse has the opposite sign and sums to zero. The inverse of -4/7 is 4/7 because -4/7 + 4/7 = 0.

mcqs.q: Ahmad was left 3/8 of a pizza and ate 1/3 of what was left. How much of the whole pizza did he eat?
mcqs.why: Working: Ahmad ate 1/3 x 3/8 = 3/24 = 1/8 of the whole pizza. So he ate 1/8 of the whole pizza.

mcqs.q: In the same pizza problem, how much of the whole pizza was left after Ahmad ate?
mcqs.why: Working: what was left for Ahmad was 3/8 and he ate 1/8, so what remained is 3/8 - 1/8 = 2/8 = 1/4 of the whole pizza.

mcqs.q: Using the same method as 1/2 + 7/9 + 1/9, what is 7/9 + 1/9?
mcqs.why: Working: the denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 7 + 1 = 8, giving 8/9. This is the first step of the full sum.

mcqs.q: Using the same method, what is 2/3 x 9/10?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply numerators and denominators: 2 x 9 = 18 and 3 x 10 = 30, giving 18/30, which simplifies by dividing by 6 to 3/5.

Question 10. Amna purchased 25/3 m cloth to stitch a shirt. If she used 13/9 m cloth to stitch the shirt. How much cloth was left with her?

(i) Question 10. Amna purchased 25/3 m cloth to stitch a shirt. If she used 13/9 m cloth to stitch the shirt. How much cloth was left with her?

Step 1: Cloth left = 25/3 - 13/9. The LCM of 3 and 9 is 9.
Step 2: 25/3 = 75/9.
Step 3: 75/9 - 13/9 = 62/9.
Final answer: 62/9 m = 6 8/9 m of cloth was left.

Question 11. If 75/4 kilogram rice is to be packed in 25/8 kilogram packets, then find

(i) (a) How many packets of rice will be packed? (b) How much rice will be there in 20 packets of mass 24/15 kilograms each?

Step 1: (a) Number of packets = (75/4) / (25/8) = 75/4 x 8/25 = 600/100 = 6.
Step 2: (b) Rice in 20 packets = 20 x 24/15 = 480/15 = 32.
Final answer: (a) 6 packets (b) 32 kilograms.

Question 12. Zara bought 235/7 litres cooking oil. She used 2 2/14 litres oil for cooking. How much oil was left with her?

(i) Question 12. Zara bought 235/7 litres cooking oil. She used 2 2/14 litres oil for cooking. How much oil was left with her?

Step 1: Oil used = 2 2/14 litres = 30/14 = 15/7 litres.
Step 2: Oil left = 235/7 - 15/7 = 220/7.
Step 3: 220/7 = 31 3/7.
Final answer: 31 3/7 litres of oil was left.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4 — Properties of Rational Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Question 1 (i). Verify the following commutative property: -3/5 + 6/7 = 6/7 + -3/5.

Step 1: Left hand side = 9/35.
Step 2: Right hand side = 9/35.
Step 3: Both sides are equal.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 9/35.

Question 1 (ii). Verify the following commutative property: 7/10 + -2/5 = -2/5 + 7/10.

Step 1: Left hand side = 3/10.
Step 2: Right hand side = 3/10.
Step 3: Both sides are equal.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 3/10.

Question 1 (iii). Verify the following commutative property: -1 1/2 x -5/7 = -5/7 x -1 1/2.

Step 1: Left hand side = 1 1/14.
Step 2: Right hand side = 1 1/14.
Step 3: Both sides are equal.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 1 1/14.

Question 1 (iv). Verify the following commutative property: 15/26 x 1/3 = 1/3 x 15/26.

Step 1: Left hand side = 5/26.
Step 2: Right hand side = 5/26.
Step 3: Both sides are equal.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 5/26.

Question 2 (i). Verify the following associative property: (1 1/3 + 2/5) + 3/7 = 1 1/3 + (2/5 + 3/7).

Step 1: Left hand side: (1 1/3 + 2/5) + 3/7 = 1 11/15 + 3/7 = 2 17/105.
Step 2: Right hand side: 1 1/3 + (2/5 + 3/7) = 1 1/3 + 29/35 = 2 17/105.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 2 17/105.

Question 2 (ii). Verify the following associative property: (5/6 + -5 1/2) + -3/4 = 5/6 + (-5 1/2 + -3/4).

Step 1: Left hand side: (5/6 + -5 1/2) + -3/4 = -4 2/3 + -3/4 = -5 5/12.
Step 2: Right hand side: 5/6 + (-5 1/2 + -3/4) = 5/6 + -6 1/4 = -5 5/12.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = -5 5/12.

Question 2 (iii). Verify the following associative property: (3/4 + -1/2) + 3/10 = 3/4 + (-1/2 + 3/10).

Step 1: Left hand side: (3/4 + -1/2) + 3/10 = 1/4 + 3/10 = 11/20.
Step 2: Right hand side: 3/4 + (-1/2 + 3/10) = 3/4 + -1/5 = 11/20.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 11/20.

Question 2 (iv). Verify the following associative property: (-1/2 + -1/2) + 1/2 = -1/2 + (-1/2 + 1/2).

Step 1: Left hand side: (-1/2 + -1/2) + 1/2 = -1 + 1/2 = -1/2.
Step 2: Right hand side: -1/2 + (-1/2 + 1/2) = -1/2 + 0 = -1/2.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = -1/2.

Question 3 (i). Verify the following distributive property: -2/5 x (1/3 + 1 1/3) = (-2/5 x 1/3) + (-2/5 x 1 1/3).

Step 1: Left hand side = -2/3.
Step 2: Right hand side = -2/3.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = -2/3.

Question 3 (ii). Verify the following distributive property: 10/11 x (6/7 + 2 1/4) = (10/11 x 6/7) + (10/11 x 2 1/4).

Step 1: Left hand side = 2 127/154.
Step 2: Right hand side = 2 127/154.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 2 127/154.

Question 3 (iii). Verify the following distributive property: 15/16 x (2/3 - 1/3) = (15/16 x 2/3) - (15/16 x 1/3).

Step 1: Left hand side = 5/16.
Step 2: Right hand side = 5/16.
Final answer: verified — L.H.S. = R.H.S. = 5/16.

Question 3 (iv). Verify the following distributive property: -2/3 x (4/5 - 4/5) = (-2/3 x 4/5) - (-2/3 x 4/5).

Step 1: Left hand side = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the value of -3/5 + 6/7, used to verify the commutative property?
mcqs.why: Working: LCM of 5 and 7 is 35: -3/5 = -21/35 and 6/7 = 30/35. Sum = (-21 + 30)/35 = 9/35, the same in either order.

mcqs.q: The commutative property for addition says which of these?
options: Grouping does not change the sum
Order does not change the sum

mcqs.q: The distributive property is shown by -2/5 x (1/3 + 1 1/3). What is the value of both sides?
mcqs.why: Working: inside the bracket 1/3 + 1 1/3 = 1 2/3 = 5/3. Then -2/5 x 5/3 = -10/15 = -2/3, matching the distributed side.

mcqs.why: Working: 2/3 - 1/3 = 1/3. Then 15/16 x 1/3 = 15/48 = 5/16, which equals the distributed calculation.

mcqs.q: What is the value of -2/3 x (4/5 - 4/5)?
mcqs.why: Working: 4/5 - 4/5 = 0 inside the bracket. Then -2/3 x 0 = 0, so both sides of the distributive verification equal 0.

mcqs.q: What is the value of 7/10 + -2/5 in the commutative verification?
mcqs.why: Working: LCM of 10 and 5 is 10: -2/5 = -4/10. Then 7/10 - 4/10 = 3/10, the same in either order.

lessons.title: Skill Practice — Rounding
lessons.notes_html:
Skill Practice — If the price of a packet of chips is Rs. 15.15, tell the price of packet of chips after rounding.

Step 2: 1 is less than 5, so the rupee figure stays 15.

Skill Practice — Round 48163 to the given degree of accuracy: (i) 2 significant figures (ii) 3 significant figures.

Step 1: (i) To 2 significant figures: the first two digits are 4 and 8, the next digit is 1, which is less than 5, so 48 stays unchanged.
Step 2: Fill the remaining places with zeros: 48000.
Step 3: (ii) To 3 significant figures: the first three digits are 4, 8 and 1, the next digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so 481 rounds up to 482.
Final answer: (i) 48000 (ii) 48200.

Skill Practice — Hamza purchased two litres of petrol for Rs. 438.75. Can you round the number to the given degree of accuracy? (i) 3 significant figures (ii) 1 decimal place.

Step 1: (i) To 3 significant figures: digits 4, 3, 8, next digit 7 is 5 or more, so 438 rounds up to 439.
Step 2: (ii) To 1 decimal place: look at the second decimal, 5, which is 5 or more, so 438.7 rounds up to 438.8.
Final answer: (i) Rs. 439 (ii) Rs. 438.8.

Skill Practice — How many significant figures does 0.0789 have?

Step 1: In a decimal number, zeros before the first non-zero digit are not significant.
Step 2: In 0.0789 the significant digits are 7, 8 and 9.
Final answer: 3 significant figures.

Skill Practice — Round -53278 to the 2 significant figures and 3 significant figures.

Step 1: Round the magnitude 53278. To 2 significant figures: digits 5 and 3, next digit 2 is less than 5, so it stays 53, giving 53000.
Step 2: To 3 significant figures: digits 5, 3 and 2, next digit 7 is 5 or more, so 532 rounds up to 533, giving 53300.
Step 3: Put the minus sign back.
Final answer: (i) -53000 (ii) -53300.

Skill Practice — Round 72/33 to the: (i) 3 decimal places (ii) 2 significant figures (iii) 3 significant figures.

Step 1: 72/33 = 2.181818...
Step 2: (i) To 3 decimal places: look at the fourth decimal, 8, which is 5 or more, so 2.181 rounds up to 2.182.
Step 3: (ii) To 2 significant figures: digits 2 and 1, next digit 8 is 5 or more, so 21 rounds up to 22, giving 2.2.
Step 4: (iii) To 3 significant figures: digits 2, 1 and 8, next digit 1 is less than 5, so it stays 2.18.
Final answer: (i) 2.182 (ii) 2.2 (iii) 2.18.

Skill Practice — 28.3 x 15.2. Find the approximated value and error. Also explain regarding the reasonableness of the solution.

Step 1: Approximated value: round the inputs to whole numbers: 28.3 becomes 28 and 15.2 becomes 15.
Step 2: Approximated product = 28 x 15 = 420.
Step 3: Accurate value = 28.3 x 15.2 = 430.16.
Step 4: Error = |430.16 - 420| = 10.16.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.5 — Rounding
lessons.notes_html:
Question 1. Round the following to the given degree of accuracy: (i) 87932 (2 significant figures) (ii) 3890 (3 significant figures) (iii) 790253 (2 significant figures) (iv) 10025 (3 significant figures) (v) 18954 (3 significant figures) (vi) 25980 (3 significant figures).

Rule: keep the required significant figures; look at the next digit — if it is 5 or more, round the last kept digit up; if less than 5, leave it unchanged; fill the remaining places with zeros.
(i) 87932 to 2 s.f.: first two digits are 8 and 7, next digit is 9, which is 5 or more, so 87 rounds up to 88.
Final answer (i): 88000.
(ii) 3890 to 3 s.f.: first three digits are 3, 8 and 9, next digit is 0, which is less than 5, so 389 stays unchanged.
Final answer (ii): 3890.
(iii) 790253 to 2 s.f.: first two digits are 7 and 9, next digit is 0, which is less than 5, so 79 stays unchanged.
Final answer (iii): 790000.
(iv) 10025 to 3 s.f.: first three digits are 1, 0 and 0, next digit is 2, which is less than 5, so 100 stays unchanged.
Final answer (iv): 10000.
(v) 18954 to 3 s.f.: first three digits are 1, 8 and 9, next digit is 5, which is 5 or more, so 189 rounds up to 190.
Final answer (v): 19000.
(vi) 25980 to 3 s.f.: first three digits are 2, 5 and 9, next digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so 259 rounds up to 260.

Rule: round the magnitude (ignore the minus sign) to the required significant figures, then put the minus sign back. 'Away from zero' only changes the result when the rounding digit is exactly 5 followed by nothing; none of these parts is an exact tie.

Final answer (i): -27.3.
(ii) |-59058| = 59058 to 2 s.f.: digits 5, 9, next digit 0 is less than 5, so it stays 59, followed by zeros.

(iii) |-12569| = 12569 to 3 s.f.: digits 1, 2, 5, next digit 6 is 5 or more, so 125 rounds up to 126.
Final answer (iii): -12600.
(iv) 17.238 to 2 s.f.: digits 1, 7, next digit 2 is less than 5, so it stays 17.
Final answer (iv): 17.
(v) 0.003857 to 3 s.f.: the significant digits start at 3, so digits are 3, 8, 5, next digit 7 is 5 or more, so 385 rounds up to 386.
Final answer (v): 0.00386.
(vi) 0.0467453 to 3 s.f.: the significant digits start at 4, so digits are 4, 6, 7, next digit 4 is less than 5, so 467 stays unchanged.

(ii) 5/27 = 0.185185... To 3 s.f.: digits are 1, 8, 5, next digit 1 is less than 5, so it stays 0.185.
Final answer (ii): 0.185.
(iii) 22/27 = 0.814814... To 3 decimal places: look at the fourth decimal, 8, which is 5 or more, so 0.814 rounds up to 0.815.
Final answer (iii): 0.815.
(iv) 27/19 = 1.421052... To 3 s.f.: digits are 1, 4, 2, next digit 1 is less than 5, so it stays 1.42.
Final answer (iv): 1.42.
(v) 37/53 = 0.698113... To 3 decimal places: look at the fourth decimal, 1, which is less than 5, so it stays 0.698.
Final answer (v): 0.698.
(vi) 77/83 = 0.927710... To 3 s.f.: digits are 9, 2, 7, next digit 7 is 5 or more, so 927 rounds up to 928.

Question 4. Round the following to the required degree of accuracy: (i) 25.359 (2 decimal places) (ii) 0.002897 (3 significant figures) (iii) 0.0878 (3 decimal places) (iv) 17.00597 (3 significant figures) (v) 0.0005246 (3 significant figures) (vi) 13.5876 (3 decimal places).

(i) 25.359 to 2 d.p.: look at the third decimal, 9, which is 5 or more, so 25.35 rounds up to 25.36.
Final answer (i): 25.36.
(ii) 0.002897 to 3 s.f.: significant digits are 2, 8, 9, next digit 7 is 5 or more, so 289 rounds up to 290.

(iii) 0.0878 to 3 d.p.: look at the fourth decimal, 8, which is 5 or more, so 0.087 rounds up to 0.088.

(iv) 17.00597 to 3 s.f.: significant digits are 1, 7, 0, next digit 0 is less than 5, so it stays 17.0.

Question 5. Compare your approximated value and accurate value. Also check is the solution reasonable or not? (i) 4.281 / 2.157 (2 decimal places) (ii) 3.348 - 2.104 (2 decimal places) (iii) 2.281 x 3.567 (2 decimal places).

Step: 4.3 / 2.2 = 1.9545..., which is 1.95 to 2 decimal places.
Step: Accurate value: 4.281 / 2.157 = 1.9846..., which is 1.98 to 2 decimal places.
Step: Difference = 1.98 - 1.95 = 0.03, which is small and of the same size as the numbers.

(ii) Approximated value: round the inputs to 1 decimal place first: 3.348 becomes 3.3 and 2.104 becomes 2.1.
Step: 3.3 - 2.1 = 1.2.
Step: Accurate value: 3.348 - 2.104 = 1.244, which is 1.24 to 2 decimal places.
Step: Difference = 1.24 - 1.20 = 0.04, which is small.

(iii) Approximated value: round the inputs to 1 decimal place first: 2.281 becomes 2.3 and 3.567 becomes 3.6.
Step: 2.3 x 3.6 = 8.28.
Step: Accurate value: 2.281 x 3.567 = 8.136327..., which is 8.14 to 2 decimal places.

lessons.title: 2.1.1 Simplification and BODMAS
lessons.notes_html:
The rule — BODMAS

To simplify an expression that contains brackets and the operations +, −, ×, ÷, follow the order BODMAS: Brackets first, then Orders (powers and roots), then Division and Multiplication (in the order they appear, from left to right), and Addition and Subtraction last (again from left to right).

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Simplification: The procedure to simplify a mathematical expression is known as simplification.

Worked example: 48 ÷ 6 × 3 + 5 − 2

Step 1: There are no brackets and no powers, so divide and multiply first, working from left to right.
Step 2: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so the expression becomes 8 × 3 + 5 − 2.
Step 3: 8 × 3 = 24, so the expression becomes 24 + 5 − 2.
Step 4: Now add and subtract from left to right: 24 + 5 = 29.
Step 5: 29 − 2 = 27.
Final answer: 27

Worked example: (15 + 9) ÷ 4 − 2 × 3

Step 1: Brackets first: 15 + 9 = 24, so the expression becomes 24 ÷ 4 − 2 × 3.
Step 2: Division: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, so the expression becomes 6 − 2 × 3.
Step 3: Multiplication: 2 × 3 = 6, so the expression becomes 6 − 6.
Step 4: Subtraction: 6 − 6 = 0.
Final answer: 0

mcqs.q: What does simplification mean?
options: Writing an expression in a larger form
The procedure to simplify a mathematical expression
Removing all numbers from an expression
mcqs.why: The book's glossary defines simplification as the procedure to simplify a mathematical expression, following a fixed order of operations.

mcqs.q: In BODMAS, which part is done first?
mcqs.why: BODMAS starts with B for Brackets, so anything inside brackets is worked out before powers, division, multiplication, addition or subtraction.

mcqs.q: In BODMAS, how are division and multiplication handled?
options: In the order they appear, from left to right
mcqs.why: Division and multiplication have equal rank in BODMAS, so they are done in the order they appear, working from left to right.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 48 / 6 * 3 + 5 - 2
mcqs.why: Working: 48 / 6 = 8, then 8 * 3 = 24, then 24 + 5 = 29, then 29 - 2 = 27. Division and multiplication come before addition and subtraction.
Working: brackets first, 15 + 9 = 24; then 24 / 4 = 6; then 2 * 3 = 6; finally 6 - 6 = 0.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 36 / 4 * 2 + 7 - 3
mcqs.why: Working: 36 / 4 = 9, then 9 * 2 = 18, then 18 + 7 = 25, then 25 - 3 = 22, doing division and multiplication from left to right first.

lessons.title: 3.1.1 Sets and Their Elements
lessons.notes_html:
What is a set?

In this world there are many things or objects which exist in collections or groups, for example a hive of bees, a bunch of flowers, a collection of different kinds of coins, a team of cricket players, a group of animals. In Mathematics, for a collection of objects or things, we use the word 'Set'. A set must be well-defined: it must be possible to decide whether any given object belongs to it or not, and its elements must be distinct (no element is written twice).

Worked example from the book (Example 1)

A = {1, 2, 3, 1} is a set or not?
Step 1: Look at the elements of A: they are 1, 2, 3 and 1 again.
Step 2: The element '1' comes twice, so the elements of the set A are not distinct.
Solution (as printed in the book): A is not a set.

Membership: ∈ and ∉

The symbol ∈ means 'belongs to' and ∉ means 'does not belong to'. In the book's Skill Practice, if A = {2, 7, 8}, we put ∈ or ∉ in the given boxes: (i) 2 ∈ A, because 2 is an element of A; (ii) 6 ∉ A, because 6 is not an element of A; (iii) 8 ∈ A, because 8 is an element of A.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Set: A set is a well-defined and distinct collection of objects/elements.

mcqs.q: What is a set?
options: Any group of objects, defined or not
A well-defined and distinct collection of objects or elements
A collection in which elements may repeat
A single object on its own
mcqs.why: The book's glossary defines a set as a well-defined and distinct collection of objects/elements, like a team of players or a bunch of flowers.

mcqs.q: A set must be well-defined. What does this mean?
options: Its elements must be numbers only
It must have more than ten elements
It must be possible to decide whether any given object belongs to it or not
Its elements must be written in order
mcqs.why: Well-defined means we can decide for any given object whether it belongs to the collection or not; collections we cannot judge exactly are not sets.

mcqs.q: Why is A = {1, 2, 3, 1} not a set?
options: It is written with curly brackets
The element 1 comes twice, so its elements are not distinct
mcqs.why: In the book's Example 1, the element 1 appears twice in {1, 2, 3, 1}. Elements of a set must be distinct, so A is not a set.

mcqs.q: What does the symbol for 'belongs to' mean?
options: It means 'is an element of' the set
It means 'is not an element of' the set
It means the two sets are equal
It means one set is a subset of another
mcqs.why: The belongs-to symbol is used when an object is an element of a set; its partner symbol, 'does not belong to', is used when the object is not an element.

mcqs.q: If A = {2, 7, 8}, which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: From the book's Skill Practice with A = {2, 7, 8}: 2 is written in A, so 2 belongs to A, while 6, 9 and 5 are not elements of A.

mcqs.q: If A = {2, 7, 8}, which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: The elements of A = {2, 7, 8} are 2, 7 and 8 only. The number 6 is not written in A, so 6 does not belong to A.

mcqs.q: Which of these collections can be a set?
mcqs.why: A set needs distinct elements with no repetition. Only {5, 10, 15, 20} has every element written exactly once; the others repeat an element.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the elements of a set is true?
options: Every element must be written twice
Elements may repeat if they are small
Repetition is allowed for letters only
mcqs.why: The book states that the elements of a set must be distinct, which means no element is written twice inside the curly brackets.

mcqs.q: A hive of bees and a team of cricket players are examples of what?
options: Collections or groups, called sets in Mathematics
mcqs.why: The lesson introduces sets through collections such as a hive of bees, a bunch of flowers and a team of cricket players; in Mathematics such a collection is called a set.

mcqs.q: If B = {a, e, i, o, u}, which is true?
options: u does not belong to B
a does not belong to B
mcqs.why: B lists the vowels a, e, i, o and u. So e belongs to B and u belongs to B, while b is not an element of B at all.

lessons.title: 3.2.1 Families of Sets and Expressing a Set
lessons.notes_html:
Some families of sets (book section 1.3.2)

  • Set of natural numbers = N = {1, 2, 3, ...}
  • Set of whole numbers = W = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}
  • Set of integers = Z = {0, ±1, ±2, ±3, ...}
  • Set of odd numbers = O = {±1, ±3, ±5, ...}
  • Set of even numbers = E = {0, ±2, ±4, ...}
  • Set of prime numbers = P = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...}

Remember (book): an empty set has no element and it is represented by { } or φ; it is also called a null set. If a set has only one element, then it is called a singleton set.

The three forms of a set (book section 1.3.3)

A set can be expressed in three ways: (a) Tabular form (roster form) — when all the elements of a set are written within curly brackets '{ }' and the elements are separated by commas, for example A = {0, 1, 3, 5, 7}, B = {a, b, c, d, e, f}, C = {10, 15, 20, 25}, D = {Raza, Hamza, Ayesha}. (b) Descriptive form — when all the elements of a set are described in words, for example A = Set of multiples of 5, B = Set of vowels in the English alphabet, C = Set of days of a week, D = Set of the first five solar months. (c) Set builder notation — the set is written by a rule, in the form {x | rule}, read as 'the set of all x such that the rule holds'. Keep in mind (book): the order of the elements in a set does not matter — A = {a, c, d, f, k} or A = {f, d, a, c, k} are the same.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Rational number: A number that can be expressed in the form of p/q where p, q are integers and q ≠ 0 is called a rational number. The set of rational number is denoted by Q.
  • LCM: The smallest common multiple of two or more than two numbers is called least common multiple (LCM).
  • Integers: The positive integers and negative integers along with zero (0) are called integers, i.e., Z = {0, ±1, ±2, ±3, ...}.

mcqs.q: The set of natural numbers N is:
mcqs.why: The book gives N = {1, 2, 3, ...}. Natural numbers start from 1; the set starting with 0 is the set of whole numbers W.

mcqs.q: The set of whole numbers W is:
mcqs.why: The book gives W = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}. Whole numbers are the natural numbers together with 0, so W starts from 0.

mcqs.q: The set of integers Z contains:
mcqs.why: The book gives Z = {0, +1, -1, +2, -2, +3, -3, ...}: the positive integers and negative integers along with zero are called integers.

mcqs.q: The set of prime numbers P begins:
mcqs.why: The book gives P = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...}. The list starts at 2, and 1, 4, 6 and 9 are not prime numbers.

mcqs.q: An empty set is represented by:
options: A blank page with no brackets
mcqs.why: The book states that an empty set has no element and is represented by { } or phi; it is also called a null set. Note {0} has one element, so it is not empty.

mcqs.q: A set with only one element is called:
mcqs.why: The book's rule: if a set has only one element, then it is called a singleton set. A set with no element is the empty or null set instead.

mcqs.q: In tabular (roster) form, a set is written by:
options: Writing all elements within curly brackets, separated by commas
mcqs.why: In tabular form all the elements are written within curly brackets '{ }' and separated by commas, for example A = {0, 1, 3, 5, 7}.

mcqs.q: 'B = Set of vowels in the English alphabet' is an example of:
mcqs.why: In descriptive form the elements of a set are described in words, as in 'Set of vowels in the English alphabet' or 'Set of days of a week'.

mcqs.q: Set builder notation is read as:
options: 'The set of all x such that the rule holds'
The list of all elements in order
The number of elements in the set
mcqs.why: In set builder notation the set is written by a rule in the form {x | rule}, read as 'the set of all x such that the rule holds'.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the order of elements in a set is true?
options: Elements must be in increasing order
Elements must be in alphabetical order
The order of the elements does not matter
The largest element must come first
mcqs.why: The book reminds us that order does not matter in a set: A = {a, c, d, f, k} and A = {f, d, a, c, k} are the same set.

lessons.title: 3.3.1 Kinds of Sets
lessons.notes_html:
Kinds of sets compared

Two sets have the same elements exactly when they are equal; they are equivalent when they merely have the same number of elements. Set A is a subset of set B when every element of A is also in B; A is a proper subset when at least one element of B is not in A, and the two sets are improper subsets of each other when each is a subset of the other (the sets are then equal). A set that contains all the elements of the sets under discussion is the universal set U. Two sets are disjoint when they have no common element, and overlapping when they have at least one common element. Subsets, unions and intersections are shown with Venn diagrams: overlapping circles inside a rectangle that represents U.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Subset: If all the elements of set A are also the elements of set B, then the set A is called the subset of B.
  • Superset: If a set A contains all the elements of a set B, then the set A is a super set of the set B.
  • Proper subset: A set A is a proper subset of a set B if all the elements of set A are elements of the set B but at least one element of the set B is not an element of set A.
  • Improper subsets: Two sets A and B are said to be subsets of each other. If set A is a subset of set B and set B is a subset of set A, then A and B are improper subsets of each other.
  • Equivalent sets: Two sets A and B are said to be equivalent if they have the same number of elements.
  • Equal sets: If sets A and B contain the same elements, then the sets A and B are equal.
  • Disjoint sets: Two or more sets are disjoint if they do not have common elements.
  • Overlapping sets: Two or more sets are overlapping if they have at least one common element.

mcqs.q: Two sets are equal when they:
options: Have the same number of elements
mcqs.why: The glossary: if sets A and B contain the same elements, then A and B are equal. Having only the same count makes them equivalent, not equal.

mcqs.q: Two sets are equivalent when they:
options: Have the same number of elements
Are drawn in one Venn diagram
mcqs.why: The glossary defines equivalent sets as two sets that have the same number of elements, even if the elements themselves are different.

mcqs.q: Set A is a subset of set B when:
options: B has fewer elements than A
A and B have no common element
A contains all the elements of B
Every element of A is also in B
mcqs.why: The glossary: if all the elements of set A are also the elements of set B, then A is called a subset of B, and B is its superset.

mcqs.q: A is a proper subset of B when:
options: Every element of A is in B, and at least one element of B is not in A
A and B are exactly equal
A has no elements at all
A and B share exactly one element
mcqs.why: A proper subset has all its elements in B, but at least one element of B is not an element of A, so the two sets cannot be equal.

mcqs.q: Two sets are improper subsets of each other when:
options: Each is a subset of the other, so the sets are equal
One is empty and the other is not
They have the same number of elements only
mcqs.why: Improper subsets: A is a subset of B and B is a subset of A. When each set is a subset of the other, the two sets are then equal.

mcqs.q: The universal set U is:
options: A set with only one element
A set that contains all the elements of the sets under discussion
The set of all prime numbers
mcqs.why: The lesson defines U as a set that contains all the elements of the sets under discussion; on a Venn diagram it is shown by the rectangle.
Working: A and B share no element at all, since {1, 2} and {3, 4} have nothing in common. Sets with no common element are disjoint sets.
Working: the element 3 belongs to both A and B, so the sets have at least one common element. Such sets are called overlapping sets.

mcqs.q: If A contains all the elements of B, then A is called the:
mcqs.why: The glossary: if a set A contains all the elements of a set B, then A is a super set (superset) of B, and B is a subset of A.

mcqs.q: On a Venn diagram, the universal set U is represented by:
mcqs.why: Venn diagrams show sets as overlapping circles inside a rectangle, and that rectangle represents the universal set U for the sets under discussion.

lessons.title: 3.4.1 Operations on Sets and the Laws of Complement
lessons.notes_html:
Operations on sets

The union A ∪ B is the set of all elements that are in A or in B (or in both). The intersection A ∩ B is the set of elements common to A and B. The difference A − B is the set of elements that are in A but not in B. The complement Aᶜ (also written A′) is the set of elements of the universal set U that are not in A: Aᶜ = U − A. On a Venn diagram, union shades both circles completely, intersection shades only the overlapping part, difference shades only the part of the first circle outside the second, and complement shades everything outside the circle.

Laws of complement

  • Laws of complement: (i) A ∪ Aᶜ = U (ii) A ∩ Aᶜ = φ (iii) (Aᶜ)ᶜ = A (iv) (A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ (v) (A ∩ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ.

mcqs.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then A union B is:
mcqs.why: Working: the union collects every element that is in A or in B, without repetition: 1, 2, 3 from A and 4, 5 extra from B, giving {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

mcqs.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then A intersection B is:
mcqs.why: Working: the intersection contains only the elements common to both sets. The only number written in both A and B is 3, so the intersection is {3}.

mcqs.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then A - B is:
mcqs.why: Working: A - B keeps the elements that are in A but not in B. Removing 3 (which is in B) from A leaves {1, 2}.

mcqs.q: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then B - A is:
mcqs.why: Working: B - A keeps the elements that are in B but not in A. Removing 3 (which is in A) from B leaves {4, 5}.

mcqs.q: If U = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} and A = {2, 4, 6}, then the complement of A is:
mcqs.why: Working: the complement is U - A, the elements of U that are not in A. Removing 2, 4 and 6 from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} leaves {1, 3, 5}.

mcqs.q: By the laws of complement, A union A' equals:
mcqs.why: Law of complement (i): A union A' = U, because every element of the universal set is either in A or in its complement, with nothing left out.

mcqs.q: By the laws of complement, A intersection A' equals:
mcqs.why: Law of complement (ii): A intersection A' = phi, because no element can be both in A and outside A at the same time.

mcqs.q: By the laws of complement, the complement of the complement of A, (A')', equals:
mcqs.why: Law of complement (iii): (A')' = A. Taking the elements outside A, and then taking what is outside that part, brings us back to A itself.

mcqs.q: By the laws of complement, (A union B)' equals:
mcqs.why: Law of complement (iv): (A union B)' = A' intersection B'. An element outside both sets must be outside A and also outside B.

mcqs.q: On a Venn diagram, the complement of A is shown by shading:
options: Only the part of A outside B
Everything outside the circle of A
mcqs.why: The lesson states that for a complement, everything outside the circle is shaded, because the complement holds all elements of U that are not in A.

lessons.title: 4.1.1 Rate, Ratio and Proportion
lessons.notes_html:
Rate and ratio

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind; it has no unit. A rate compares two quantities of different kinds, so a rate always carries a unit (for example rupees per day, or km per hour). The ratio a : b is written as the fraction a/b, and a ratio is simplified by dividing both terms by their HCF, exactly like a fraction.

Proportion

An equality of two ratios is called a proportion, written a : b :: c : d. In a proportion, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means: a × d = b × c. This rule is used to find a missing term of a proportion. Quantities are in direct proportion when both increase (or both decrease) together in the same ratio, and in inverse proportion when one increases as the other decreases.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Rate: The rate is a ratio of two quantities having different units.
  • Ratio: The ratio is a ratio of two quantities having different units. (Glossary, as printed.)
  • Proportion: An equality of two ratios is called a proportion.
  • Direct proportion: Two quantities are said to be in direct proportion if an increase or decrease in one quantity causes the increase or decrease in the other quantity in the same ratio.
  • Inverse proportion: Two quantities are said to be in inverse proportion if the increase or decrease in one quantity causes the decrease or increase in the other quantity in the same ratio.

The same kind, and it has no unit

options: The same kind, with no unit
The same kind, with a unit
Different kinds, so it always carries a unit
mcqs.why: A rate compares quantities of different kinds, for example rupees per day or km per hour, so a rate always carries a unit.

mcqs.why: The lesson states that the ratio a : b is written as the fraction a/b, and it is simplified like a fraction by dividing both terms by their HCF.

mcqs.why: Working: the HCF of 12 and 18 is 6. Dividing both terms by 6 gives 12/6 : 18/6 = 2 : 3, the simplest form of the ratio.

mcqs.why: The glossary defines a proportion as an equality of two ratios, written in the form a : b :: c : d with the :: symbol between the ratios.

mcqs.why: In a : b :: c : d, the first and last terms, a and d, are the extremes, while the middle terms b and c are the means.

mcqs.q: In a proportion, the product of the extremes equals:
mcqs.why: The key rule of proportion: product of extremes = product of means, that is a * d = b * c. This rule is used to find a missing term.

options: No, because 2 * 6 is not equal to 3 * 4
No, because the terms are different
Yes, because all terms are even
mcqs.why: Working: product of extremes = 2 * 6 = 12 and product of means = 3 * 4 = 12. The products are equal, so 2 : 3 :: 4 : 6 is a proportion.

mcqs.why: Working: product of extremes = product of means, so 3 * 15 = 5 * x, giving 45 = 5x and x = 45 / 5 = 9.

One increases as the other decreases
mcqs.why: The glossary: in inverse proportion, an increase or decrease in one quantity causes the decrease or increase in the other quantity in the same ratio.

lessons.title: 5.1.1 Profit, Loss and Discount
lessons.notes_html:
Profit and loss

The price at which an item is bought is its cost price (C.P) and the price at which it is sold is its selling price (S.P). When S.P > C.P there is a profit = S.P − C.P; when C.P > S.P there is a loss = C.P − S.P. Percentages are always found on the cost price:

Profit % = (Profit ÷ C.P) × 100
Loss % = (Loss ÷ C.P) × 100

Discount and taxes

A discount is the reduction offered on the marked price; the selling price = marked price − discount. Zakat is charged at 2.5% of the total wealth; ushr is charged at 5% on land irrigated by artificial resources and 10% on land irrigated by natural sources. Income tax, property tax and sales tax are worked out as percentages of the income, the property value and the price of the item.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Cost price: The price at which an item is bought is called its cost price.
  • Selling price: The price at which an item is sold is called its selling price.
  • Discount: The reduction or cut offered on the marked price is called the discount.
  • Income tax: Income tax is the tax imposed by the government on the income of individuals exceeding a certain amount.
  • Property tax: Property tax is a tax imposed by government on the properties such as houses, land and shops.
  • Sales tax: When a customer purchases an item, he/she pays an extra amount in addition to the original price of the item. This extra amount is called general sales tax.
  • Zakat: The rate of zakat is 2.5% of the total wealth.
  • Ushr: The rate of ushr is 5% and 10% depending on the land irrigated by natural sources or artificial resources respectively.

lessons.title: 6.1.1 Squares, Square Roots and Estimation
lessons.notes_html:
Squares and square roots

The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself: for example 13² = 13 × 13 = 169. The square root of a number is the value which, multiplied by itself, gives the number back: √169 = 13. Numbers such as 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... are perfect squares. The square roots of perfect squares are found by prime factorisation: pair the equal prime factors and take one factor from each pair. The square root of a fraction is the square root of the numerator over the square root of the denominator, and the square root of a decimal is found by making the number of decimal places even and then working place by place.

Estimation

To estimate a square root, find the two perfect squares between which the number lies: for example 90 lies between 81 and 100, so √90 lies between 9 and 10, closer to 9; a closer estimate is 9.5. The error is the difference between the actual value and the approximate (estimated) value.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Error: The difference between the actual value and approximate/estimated value is called an error.

mcqs.q: What is the square of 13?
mcqs.why: The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself: 13^2 = 13 x 13 = 169, as worked in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What is sqrt(169)?
mcqs.why: The square root of a number is the value which, multiplied by itself, gives the number back: 13 x 13 = 169, so sqrt(169) = 13.

mcqs.q: Which of the following numbers is a perfect square?
mcqs.why: Perfect squares are numbers like 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... Here 36 = 6 x 6 = 6^2, while 18, 27 and 50 are not the square of any whole number.

mcqs.q: Using prime factorisation, find sqrt(144).
mcqs.why: 144 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. Pair the equal prime factors and take one from each pair: 2 x 2 x 3 = 12, so sqrt(144) = 12.

mcqs.q: Find sqrt(25/49).
mcqs.why: The square root of a fraction is the square root of the numerator over the square root of the denominator: sqrt(25)/sqrt(49) = 5/7.

mcqs.q: Between which two whole numbers does sqrt(90) lie?
mcqs.why: 90 lies between the perfect squares 81 and 100, and sqrt(81) = 9 and sqrt(100) = 10, so sqrt(90) lies between 9 and 10.

mcqs.q: A closer estimate of sqrt(90), as given in the lesson, is:
mcqs.why: 90 lies between 81 and 100, closer to 9 than to 10 on the number line of squares, and the lesson gives the closer estimate of sqrt(90) as 9.5.

mcqs.q: In estimation, what is meant by the error?
options: The square of the estimated value
The difference between the actual value and the approximate (estimated) value
The sum of the actual and estimated values
The product of the actual and estimated values
mcqs.why: The book's glossary defines error as the difference between the actual value and the approximate/estimated value.

mcqs.q: What is the square of 15?
mcqs.why: The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself: 15^2 = 15 x 15 = 225.

mcqs.why: For a decimal, make the number of decimal places even and work place by place: 0.09 has two decimal places and 0.3 x 0.3 = 0.09, so sqrt(0.09) = 0.3.

lessons.title: 7.1.1 Term to Term Rule and General Term
lessons.notes_html:
Term to term rule

A sequence is an ordered list of numbers. The term to term rule tells how the next term is obtained from the previous term. In the book's Example 1: (i) 2, 5, 8, 11, __, __, __, 23 — the difference between the 1st and 2nd term is 3 (5 − 2 = 3) and 3 is added to each term, so the 5th term = 11 + 3 = 14, the 6th term = 14 + 3 = 17 and the 7th term = 17 + 3 = 20; hence 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23. (ii) 1, 3, 7, 13, __, 31 — the difference between the 1st and 2nd term is 2, and 2 is added continuously to the next difference (+2, +4, +6, +8, +10), so the 5th term = 13 + 8 = 21; hence 1, 3, 7, 13, 21, 31.

More patterns from the book

The sequence 23, −23, 23, −23, 23 shows that the next term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by (−1), so the next terms are −23, 23, −23. The sequence 500000, −50000, 5000, −500, 50 shows that each term is obtained by dividing the previous term by (−10), so the next terms are −5 and 0.5.

The general term

The position-to-term rule is written with the general term aₙ: for example, if a₁ = 3, a₂ = 5, a₃ = 8 and a₄ = 12, the differences grow by 1 each time, and any term can be found from its position. A number pattern that grows by adding or subtracting the same amount again and again is checked term by term before the missing terms are written.

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Term rule: The term to term rule is used for a sequence in which the next term is obtained from the previous terms.
  • General term: The nᵗʰ term of the sequence is also known as general term of the sequence and is written as aₙ.

mcqs.q: In the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, __, the 5th term is:
mcqs.why: The difference between consecutive terms is 3 (5 - 2 = 3), so 3 is added to each term: the 5th term = 11 + 3 = 14.

mcqs.q: What is the term to term rule of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, ...?
mcqs.why: Check the differences: 5 - 2 = 3, 8 - 5 = 3, 11 - 8 = 3. The same amount 3 is added each time, so the rule is add 3.

mcqs.q: In the sequence 1, 3, 7, 13, __, 31, the missing 5th term is:
mcqs.why: The differences grow by 2 each time: +2, +4, +6, +8, +10. So the 5th term = 13 + 8 = 21, and then 21 + 10 = 31 confirms the pattern.

mcqs.q: The sequence 23, -23, 23, -23, 23, ... is formed by multiplying each term by -1. What is the 6th term?
mcqs.why: Each term is the previous term multiplied by (-1), so the signs alternate: the 6th term = 23 x (-1) = -23.

mcqs.q: In the sequence 500000, -50000, 5000, -500, 50, ..., each term is found by dividing the previous term by -10. What is the next term?
mcqs.why: Divide the last given term by -10: 50 / (-10) = -5, following the term to term rule stated in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Continuing the sequence 500000, -50000, 5000, -500, 50, -5, ..., what is the term after -5?
mcqs.why: Each term is the previous term divided by -10: (-5) / (-10) = 0.5, so the term after -5 is 0.5.

mcqs.q: The general term (n-th term) of a sequence is written as:
mcqs.why: The glossary states that the n-th term of the sequence is also known as the general term and is written as a_n.

mcqs.q: What is a sequence?
options: The sum of all its terms
A list of numbers in any random order
mcqs.why: The lesson defines a sequence as an ordered list of numbers, where the term to term rule tells how each next term is obtained.

mcqs.q: What does the term to term rule tell us?
options: How to add all the terms together
How the last term is found from the first term
How many terms the sequence has
How the next term is obtained from the previous term
mcqs.why: The glossary states the term to term rule is used for a sequence in which the next term is obtained from the previous term.

mcqs.q: For a sequence with a_1 = 3, a_2 = 5, a_3 = 8 and a_4 = 12, the differences grow by 1 each time. What is a_5?
mcqs.why: Differences: 5 - 3 = 2, 8 - 5 = 3, 12 - 8 = 4, growing by 1 each time. The next difference is 5, so a_5 = 12 + 5 = 17.

lessons.title: 8.1.1 Algebraic Expressions, Terms and Polynomials
lessons.notes_html:
Expressions, terms, variables and constants

An algebraic expression connects variables and constants by the operations +, −, ×, ÷. Each part of an expression separated by + or − is a term; a term that can take various values is a variable, and a term with a fixed value is a constant. Terms with the same variable part are like terms (for example 3x² and 8x²); terms with different variable parts are unlike terms and cannot be added or subtracted.

Polynomials and their operations

A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the exponent of the variable is a whole number; polynomials with one, two and three terms are called monomials, binomials and trinomials. Polynomials are added and subtracted by combining like terms; they are multiplied term by term using the laws of exponents (aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ), and divided term by term (aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ). The square of a binomial uses the identities (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², and a difference of squares factorises as a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Key terms from the book's Glossary

  • Algebraic expression: An expression which connects variables and constants by mathematical operations (+, −, ×, ÷) is called an algebraic expression.
  • Variable: A term which can take various numerical values is called variable.
  • Constant: A term which cannot be changed and has a fixed value is called constant.
  • An equation: An equation is a statement which shows the equal value of both the expressions.
  • An inequality: An inequality is a statement which shows that an expression is less than or greater than the other.
  • Polynomial: A polynomial is an algebraic expression comprising of whole number as exponent of the variable. A polynomial consists of variables, coefficient and constant.
  • Types of polynomials: There are three types of polynomials i.e. monomials, binomials and trinomials.
  • Open sentence: A sentence which has one or more unknown is called open sentence.

mcqs.q: What is an algebraic expression?
options: An expression which connects variables and constants by operations +, -, x and /
A statement which shows two expressions have equal value
A term which has a fixed value and cannot be changed
A sentence which has one or more unknowns
mcqs.why: By definition, an algebraic expression connects variables and constants by mathematical operations such as +, -, x and /. An equality statement is an equation, not an expression.

mcqs.q: In the expression 5x + 7, which part is the variable term?
mcqs.why: A variable is a term which can take various numerical values. In 5x + 7, x can take different values, so 5x is the variable term and 7 is fixed.

mcqs.q: In the expression 3y - 4, what is the constant?
mcqs.why: A constant is a term which cannot be changed and has a fixed value. Here 3y changes with y, while -4 always stays -4, so the constant is -4.

mcqs.q: Which pair consists of like terms?
mcqs.why: Like terms have exactly the same variable part. Both 3x^2 and 8x^2 have variable part x^2, so they are like terms and can be added or subtracted.

mcqs.q: Which pair consists of unlike terms?
mcqs.why: Unlike terms have different variable parts. 6x has variable part x and 9y has variable part y, so they are unlike and cannot be added or subtracted.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in the expression 4x^2 - 2y + 8?
mcqs.why: Terms are the parts separated by + or -. Step 1: split 4x^2 - 2y + 8 at the signs. Step 2: the parts are 4x^2, -2y and 8, which makes 3 terms in total.

mcqs.q: A polynomial with exactly two terms is called a:
mcqs.why: Polynomials are named by their number of terms: one term is a monomial, two terms form a binomial, and three terms form a trinomial. So two terms give a binomial.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a monomial?
mcqs.why: A monomial has only one term. 4xy is a single term, while x + y has 2 terms, 2xyz + 20 has 2 terms, and x^2 - 2xy + 16 has 3 terms.

mcqs.q: What must be true about the exponent of the variable in a polynomial?
options: It must be a whole number
mcqs.why: A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the exponent of the variable is a whole number such as 0, 1, 2 or 3. Negative or fractional powers are not allowed.

mcqs.q: Using (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, what is (x + 3)^2?
mcqs.why: Step 1: put a = x and b = 3 in (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2. Step 2: x^2 + 2(x)(3) + 3^2. Step 3: simplify to x^2 + 6x + 9.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in the expression 4xy?
mcqs.why: Step 1: count the parts separated by + or -. Step 2: 4xy has no + or - sign separating parts, so it is a single term. The number of terms is 1.

mcqs.q: In the expression 2xyz + 20, what is the constant?
mcqs.why: A constant has a fixed value. In 2xyz + 20, the term 2xyz changes when x, y or z changes, while 20 never changes, so the constant is 20.

mcqs.q: In the expression x^2 - 2xy + 16, which are the variables?
mcqs.why: Variables are the letters that can take various values. In x^2 - 2xy + 16 the letters are x and y, while 16 is the constant, so the variables are x and y.

mcqs.q: Which statement is an open sentence?
mcqs.why: An open sentence has one or more unknowns. x + 5 = 12 contains the unknown x, while the other three are complete number statements with no unknown, so they are close sentences.

mcqs.q: Which pair are like terms?
mcqs.why: Like terms have exactly the same variable part. 4x^2y and 7yx^2 both have variable part x^2y (yx^2 = x^2y), so they are like terms.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an inequality?
mcqs.why: An inequality shows that an expression is less than or greater than another, using signs like < or >. x - 2 > 7 uses >, while the others use = and are equations.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an equation?
mcqs.why: An equation is a statement which shows the equal value of both expressions, so it must contain the = sign. Only 2x - 5 = 11 has =, the others are inequalities.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in x^2 - 2xy + 16?
mcqs.why: Step 1: split the expression at the + and - signs. Step 2: the parts are x^2, -2xy and +16. Step 3: counting them gives 3 terms in total.

mcqs.q: In the expression 4x^2 - 2y + 8, what is the constant?
mcqs.why: The constant is the term with a fixed value that does not contain a variable. In 4x^2 - 2y + 8, the terms with variables are 4x^2 and -2y, leaving 8 as the constant.

mcqs.q: Which pair are like terms?
mcqs.why: Like terms must have the same variable and the same power. Both (3/2)x^2 and (9/2)x^2 have variable part x^2; only their coefficients differ, so they are like terms.

lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Which of the following are polynomials?

Step 1: A polynomial has whole-number exponents of the variable only — no negative or fractional powers and no variable in a denominator.
Final answer: (i), (ii), (iv), (vi), (vii) are polynomials (key)

Q2. State the degree of each polynomial

Step 1: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable in it.
Final answer: (i) 2; (ii) 2; (iii) 3; (iv) 2; (v) 3; (vi) 1; (vii) 4; (viii) 2 (key)

Q3. Add the polynomials

Step 1: Add like terms column by column: x-powers with x-powers, and constants with constants.
Final answer: (i) 10x2 − 3x + 16; (ii) 7x2 + 10x + 9; (iii) 4x3 + 4x2 + 7x + 8; (iv) 6x2 − 2x + 25; (v) 5x3 + 3x2 + 23x + 17

Q4. Subtract the polynomials

Step 1: Change the sign of every term of the polynomial being subtracted, then add like terms.
Final answer: (i) 5x3 + 6x + 8; (ii) 7y2 + 8q2 + 4r; (iii) 5x3 − 12x2 + 8x + 12; (iv) 8x3 + 9x2 + 5x + 8

Q5. Simplify

Step 1: Remove the brackets (a minus before a bracket changes every sign inside), then collect like terms.
Final answer: (i) 5x2 + 2x2 + 5x + 10 (Q5, as printed); (v) 3x3 + x2y + 3xy2 + 3y3; (vi) 7z + y + 13 (and (i) 3x2 + 12x + 5 (Q6) for Q6 (i))

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial?
mcqs.why: A polynomial has only whole-number exponents of the variable. x^(-1) has exponent -1, which is negative, so x^(-1) + 2 is not a polynomial.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x^3 + 2x + 9?
mcqs.why: Step 1: list the powers of x: 3 in 5x^3, 1 in 2x, and 0 in 9. Step 2: the degree is the highest power, which is 3.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 7x^4 - 3x^2 + x?
mcqs.why: Step 1: the powers of x are 4, 2 and 1. Step 2: the degree of a polynomial is its highest power of the variable, so the degree is 4.
Step 1: add like terms: 3x^2 + 7x^2 = 10x^2. Step 2: 2x - 5x = -3x. Step 3: 5 + 11 = 16. Result: 10x^2 - 3x + 16.
Step 1: 2x^2 + 5x^2 = 7x^2. Step 2: 4x + 6x = 10x. Step 3: 3 + 6 = 9. Adding like terms gives 7x^2 + 10x + 9.
Step 1: change signs of the second polynomial: -(3x^2 + 2x + 4) = -3x^2 - 2x - 4. Step 2: 8x^2 - 3x^2 = 5x^2, 5x - 2x = 3x, 10 - 4 = 6. Result: 5x^2 + 3x + 6.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 5x^2 + 3x - 2x^2 + 2x
mcqs.why: Step 1: collect x^2 terms: 5x^2 - 2x^2 = 3x^2. Step 2: collect x terms: 3x + 2x = 5x. Step 3: the simplified form is 3x^2 + 5x.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 4x + 9?
mcqs.why: Step 1: 4x has power 1 and the constant 9 has power 0. Step 2: the highest power is 1, so this linear polynomial has degree 1.

mcqs.q: Subtract: (6x^2 - x + 12) - (x^2 + x - 3)
Simplify by removing brackets: 10 - (3x - 5)
mcqs.why: Step 1: a minus before a bracket changes every sign inside: -(3x - 5) = -3x + 5. Step 2: 10 - 3x + 5 = -3x + 15 after collecting the constants.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 4x^2 x 8xy
mcqs.why: Step 1: multiply coefficients: 4 x 8 = 32. Step 2: multiply x powers: x^2 x x = x^(2+1) = x^3, and y stays y. Result: 32x^3y.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 3x^3 x 8x^2y^5
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficients: 3 x 8 = 24. Step 2: x^3 x x^2 = x^(3+2) = x^5 using a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). Step 3: y^5 is unchanged. Result: 24x^5y^5.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 2x x 7x^7y^6
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficients: 2 x 7 = 14. Step 2: x x x^7 = x^(1+7) = x^8. Step 3: y^6 is unchanged. Result: 14x^8y^6.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (2xy^2) x (4x^6y^5)
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficients: 2 x 4 = 8. Step 2: x x x^6 = x^7. Step 3: y^2 x y^5 = y^(2+5) = y^7. Result: 8x^7y^7.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 3x^2(2x^3 + 5xy^3)
mcqs.why: Step 1: distribute 3x^2 over both terms of the bracket. Step 2: 3x^2 x 2x^3 = 6x^5. Step 3: 3x^2 x 5xy^3 = 15x^3y^3, since x^2 x x = x^3 and y^3 is unchanged. Result: 6x^5 + 15x^3y^3.

mcqs.q: Using a^m x a^n = a^(m+n), what is x^4 x x^3?
mcqs.why: Step 1: when multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents. Step 2: 4 + 3 = 7. Step 3: so x^4 x x^3 = x^7.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 5l^2 x 2l^3m^7
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficients: 5 x 2 = 10. Step 2: l^2 x l^3 = l^(2+3) = l^5. Step 3: m^7 is unchanged. Result: 10l^5m^7.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 2x^2y(5y^2 + 8xy^3)
mcqs.why: Step 1: distribute 2x^2y. Step 2: 2x^2y x 5y^2 = 10x^2y^3. Step 3: 2x^2y x 8xy^3 = 16x^3y^4, since y x y^3 = y^4. Result: 10x^2y^3 + 16x^3y^4.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (3m^2n) x (2m n^2)
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficients: 3 x 2 = 6. Step 2: m^2 x m = m^3. Step 3: n x n^2 = n^3. Result: 6m^3n^3.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 7a(2a^3 - 5b)
mcqs.why: Step 1: distribute 7a over the bracket. Step 2: 7a x 2a^3 = 14a^4. Step 3: 7a x (-5b) = -35ab. Result: 14a^4 - 35ab.

mcqs.q: Divide: 12x^5 / 3x^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: divide coefficients: 12 / 3 = 4. Step 2: subtract powers using a^m / a^n = a^(m-n): x^(5-2) = x^3. Result: 4x^3.

mcqs.q: Divide: 20x^4y^6 / 5x y^2
Divide term by term: (8x^3 - 4x^2) / 2x
mcqs.why: Step 1: 8x^3 / 2x = 4x^2. Step 2: -4x^2 / 2x = -2x. Step 3: dividing term by term gives 4x^2 - 2x.

mcqs.q: Using a^m / a^n = a^(m-n), what is x^9 / x^4?
mcqs.why: Step 1: when dividing powers of the same base, subtract the exponents. Step 2: 9 - 4 = 5. Step 3: so x^9 / x^4 = x^5.
Step 1: 12m^3 / 3m = 4m^2. Step 2: -18m^2 / 3m = -6m. Step 3: term-by-term division gives 4m^2 - 6m.

mcqs.q: Divide: 6x^5 / 2x
mcqs.why: Step 1: divide coefficients: 6 / 2 = 3. Step 2: subtract powers using a^m / a^n = a^(m-n): x^(5-1) = x^4. Step 3: the result is 3x^4.

mcqs.q: Divide: (10x^2 - 6x) / 2
mcqs.why: Step 1: divide each term by 2: 10x^2 / 2 = 5x^2. Step 2: -6x / 2 = -3x. Step 3: the result is 5x^2 - 3x.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 5x times x^3y^4
mcqs.why: Step 1: coefficient stays 5 (5 x 1 = 5). Step 2: x x x^3 = x^(1+3) = x^4. Step 3: y^4 is unchanged. Result: 5x^4y^4.

mcqs.q: Divide: 16a^5b^4 / 4a^2b
Divide term by term: (6x - 4y - 10) / 2
mcqs.why: Step 1: 6x / 2 = 3x. Step 2: -4y / 2 = -2y. Step 3: -10 / 2 = -5. Result: 3x - 2y - 5.

mcqs.q: Expand using (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2: (2x + 5y)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 2x, b = 5y. Step 2: a^2 = 4x^2, 2ab = 2(2x)(5y) = 20xy, b^2 = 25y^2. Step 3: sum is 4x^2 + 20xy + 25y^2.

mcqs.q: Expand using (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2: (3x - 4)^2
Expand: (5l + 2m)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: square first term: (5l)^2 = 25l^2. Step 2: twice product: 2(5l)(2m) = 20lm. Step 3: square second term: (2m)^2 = 4m^2. Sum: 25l^2 + 20lm + 4m^2.

mcqs.q: Expand: (3x - 2y)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 3x, b = 2y in (a - b)^2. Step 2: a^2 = 9x^2, -2ab = -2(3x)(2y) = -12xy, b^2 = 4y^2. Step 3: result is 9x^2 - 12xy + 4y^2.

mcqs.q: Use (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2 to expand (x + 2y)(x - 2y)
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = x, b = 2y. Step 2: a^2 = x^2 and b^2 = (2y)^2 = 4y^2. Step 3: difference of squares gives x^2 - 4y^2.

mcqs.q: Expand: (7x + y)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: (7x)^2 = 49x^2. Step 2: 2(7x)(y) = 14xy. Step 3: y^2 = y^2. Step 4: sum is 49x^2 + 14xy + y^2.

mcqs.q: Expand: (m^2 - n)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = m^2, b = n. Step 2: a^2 = m^4, -2ab = -2(m^2)(n) = -2m^2n, b^2 = n^2. Step 3: result is m^4 - 2m^2n + n^2.

mcqs.q: Use a^2 - b^2 to expand (m^2 + n^2)(m^2 - n^2)
mcqs.why: Step 1: treat a = m^2 and b = n^2. Step 2: a^2 = (m^2)^2 = m^4 and b^2 = (n^2)^2 = n^4. Step 3: (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2 = m^4 - n^4.

mcqs.q: Expand: (x + 4)^2
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = x, b = 4. Step 2: a^2 = x^2, 2ab = 2(x)(4) = 8x, b^2 = 16. Step 3: sum is x^2 + 8x + 16.

mcqs.q: Which identity gives a^2 - 2ab + b^2?
mcqs.why: The square of a difference expands as (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2: square the first, subtract twice the product, and add the square of the second term.

mcqs.q: Factorise by taking out the HCF: 6xy - 14yz
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF of 6xy and 14yz is 2y. Step 2: 6xy / 2y = 3x and -14yz / 2y = -7z. Step 3: write as 2y(3x - 7z). Check: 2y x 3x = 6xy, 2y x (-7z) = -14yz.

mcqs.q: Factorise: 30x^4 - 45x^2y
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF of coefficients 30 and 45 is 15, and of x powers is x^2, so HCF = 15x^2. Step 2: 30x^4 / 15x^2 = 2x^2, -45x^2y / 15x^2 = -3y. Result: 15x^2(2x^2 - 3y).

mcqs.q: Factorise: 6x^2y - 24yz
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF of 6x^2y and 24yz is 6y. Step 2: 6x^2y / 6y = x^2 and -24yz / 6y = -4z. Step 3: factorised form is 6y(x^2 - 4z).

mcqs.q: Factorise: 5x^5 - 10x^4 + 15x^3
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF is 5x^3 (5 is HCF of 5,10,15 and x^3 is lowest power). Step 2: divide each term: x^2, -2x, +3. Step 3: result is 5x^3(x^2 - 2x + 3).

mcqs.q: Factorise by grouping: x^2 + 5x - 2x - 10 grouped as x(x + 5) - 2(x + 5) gives:
mcqs.why: Step 1: group pairs: x^2 + 5x = x(x + 5) and -2x - 10 = -2(x + 5). Step 2: the common bracket (x + 5) factors out. Step 3: result is (x - 2)(x + 5).

mcqs.q: Which expression is obtained by expanding 7x(x^3 - 2xy + 3y^3)?
mcqs.why: Step 1: multiply 7x by each term: 7x x x^3 = 7x^4. Step 2: 7x x (-2xy) = -14x^2y. Step 3: 7x x 3y^3 = 21xy^3. So expanding gives 7x^4 - 14x^2y + 21xy^3, and reversing this gives the factorisation.

mcqs.q: Factorise by grouping: ax - ay + bx - by after grouping gives (a + b)(x - y) - which step is correct first?
options: Take x common from all terms
Group a(x - y) + b(x - y), then factor (x - y)
Take y common from all terms
mcqs.why: Step 1: group as (ax - ay) + (bx - by) = a(x - y) + b(x - y). Step 2: the same bracket (x - y) appears in both parts. Step 3: factor it out to get (a + b)(x - y).

mcqs.q: Factorise: 9p^2q^2 - 18pq + 27p^3q^4
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF is 9pq. Step 2: divide: 9p^2q^2/9pq = pq, -18pq/9pq = -2, 27p^3q^4/9pq = 3p^2q^3. Step 3: result is 9pq(pq - 2 + 3p^2q^3).

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 12x^3 and 18x^2y?
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF of coefficients 12 and 18 is 6. Step 2: lowest power of x present in both is x^2, and y is not in both. Step 3: HCF = 6x^2.

mcqs.q: Factorise: 4x^3 - 8x^2y^3 + 12x^2y
mcqs.why: Step 1: HCF is 4x^2. Step 2: divide each term: 4x^3/4x^2 = x, -8x^2y^3/4x^2 = -2y^3, 12x^2y/4x^2 = 3y. Step 3: result is 4x^2(x - 2y^3 + 3y).
